captions.linkedin:
Da, Gurun and Warachka (2014, RFS) split momentum in 2 and only 1 half actually worked. 📊

Standard momentum lumps every winner together. The Frog-in-the-Pan paper asked a sharper question: did the winner creep up day after day, or get there by a few violent jumps?

Continuous-information momentum (slow daily drift) earned +5.94% in the paper. Discrete-information momentum (a few big jumps) earned -2.07%. Same 12-1 formation, opposite outcomes.

The mechanism is limited attention. A 1% jump hits the news. A 0.1% drift over 60 sessions is the same move, and almost nobody notices.

Here's the complete logic. No black box:

🔹 12-1 FORMATION, skip the most recent month.
🔹 INFO DISCRETENESS, score each stock by the fraction of up-vs-down days.
🔹 CONTINUOUS FILTER, keep only the steady-drip names.
🔹 LONG WINNERS / SHORT LOSERS, inside the continuous bucket.
🔹 6-MONTH HOLD, continuous-info momentum does not reverse.
🔹 LOW-COVERAGE TILT, neglected names show the strongest drift.

If you already run momentum, this is a single filter that strips out the slice most likely to mean-revert.
